clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: The deep autoencoder successfully generated significantly higher deviation metrics in patients with schizophrenia (p=.001) and autism spectrum disorder (p<.001) compared to healthy controls, and revealed distinct patterns of neuroanatomical alterations for each disorder consistent with existing literature, though with modest classification performance (AUC-ROC: 0.707 for SCZ, 0.639 for ASD).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: The deep autoencoder trained on 1,113 healthy controls from HCP achieved a mean reconstruction error of 0.32 on the training set. When applied to the NUSDAST dataset, it yielded significantly higher deviation metrics in schizophrenia patients (1.14±0.28) compared to healthy controls (0.97±0.23) with Cliff's delta=0.4142 and p=.001. In the ABIDE dataset, autism spectrum disorder patients showed higher deviation (1.27±0.40) than controls (1.09±0.30) with Cliff's delta=0.2764 and p<.001. Regional analysis revealed disorder-specific patterns: for schizophrenia, the most altered regions included left ventral diencephalon (effect size=0.417), left lateral ventricle (0.410), right superior temporal cortex (0.387), right lateral ventricle (0.328), and left precentral cortex (0.318); for autism, the most altered regions were left choroid plexus (0.250), right cuneus (0.245), left putamen (0.228), and left cerebellum cortex (0.222). Classification performance was modest with AUC-ROC of 0.707 (95% CI: 0.662-0.751) for schizophrenia and 0.639 (95% CI: 0.611-0.666) for autism, comparable to or slightly better than linear SVM classifiers (AUC-ROC: 0.637 and 0.569, respectively). The model successfully predicted age with MAE of 3.40 years (HC) and 3.57 years (SCZ) in NUSDAST, and 4.02 years (HC) and 3.83 years (ASD) in ABIDE; sex prediction accuracy was 75.00% (HC) and 62.28% (SCZ) in NUSDAST, and 79.04% (HC) and 78.31% (ASD) in ABIDE. Comparison with PCA-based linear approach showed that the deep autoencoder achieved larger effect sizes despite PCA having lower reconstruction error on healthy subjects.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is an early application of deep learning-based normative modeling in neuropsychiatry using structural MRI. The study demonstrates proof-of-concept for using autoencoders to quantify neuroanatomical deviations at individual level across different disorders. The HCP training cohort age range (22-37 years) is relatively narrow, limiting generalizability to pediatric and elderly populations. Clinical datasets were restricted to the same age range. The semi-supervised approach incorporating age and sex is innovative but not standard practice in neuroimaging. Supplementary materials include comprehensive regional analyses, comparison with PCA linear method, saliency map interpretations, and mass-univariate analyses for comparison. Model architecture selection via 10-fold CV tested configurations from 25-10-25 to 100-75-100 neurons, with 100-75-100 (plus input/output layers) selected as optimal. Training used Adam optimizer with exponential learning rate decay (0.05 to 0.0005 over 2,000 epochs), mini-batch size 64, additive Gaussian noise (mean=0, SD=0.1) for denoising. The study acknowledges that the deep neural network resembles a 'black box' despite attempts at interpretation via saliency maps. Notable that several regions significant in the normative approach were not significant in mass-univariate analysis and vice versa, highlighting the multivariate nature capturing inter-regional correlations beyond volume/thickness differences alone.
